learning.why: Teacher showed whole=4 and asked eaten out of all four, not out of leftovers. Child now repeats that 2 out of 4 is correct.
The teacher's whiteboard and previous example directly showed bottom number counts all equal pieces in the whole, not leftovers.

end.summary: Practised fractions as equal shares using shapes, sweets, bananas, cake and chocolate.
end.parentNote: Nisha practised naming halves, thirds and quarters by checking that parts are equal, and comparing unit fractions from the same whole. They correctly shared quantities into equal groups and explained that 1/2 is larger than 1/4 when the whole is the same. There was a mix-up between the parts taken or left and the total parts in the whole; Nisha later said the denominator should come from all four pieces, but this idea was not yet secure. At home, fold paper into 2, 3 and 4 equal parts and ask Nisha to name one part and the whole number of parts.
